faqs.q: What is the minimum salary in Australia for a full-time adult worker?
faqs.a: The minimum salary in Australia for an adult employee not covered by an award or agreement is based on the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, that is $26.44 per hour. bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the minimum salary in Australia

When you're comparing job offers or planning your budget, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is essential. In Australia, the standard full-time working week is 38 hours, and the year is calculated over 52 weeks. This article explains how to calculate your minimum salary in Australia, what the National Minimum Wage is, and how casual loading, superannuation, and tax affect your take-home pay.

### The National Minimum Wage

The Fair Work Ombudsman sets the National Minimum Wage each year after the Annual Wage Review by the Fair Work Commission. As of 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. This applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. If you are covered by an award, your minimum pay is likely higher.

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For the National Minimum Wage: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80 per year.

This is the gross amount before tax and before superannuation (which is paid on top).

### Award and agreement rates

Most Australian employees are covered by a modern award or an enterprise agreement. Awards set minimum pay rates for specific industries and occupations, and these rates are often higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, the Hospitality Industry General Award or the Clerks Private Sector Award have different classification levels with their own hourly rates. You can find the correct pay guide for your award on the [pay guides](/blog) page.

If you are covered by an enterprise agreement, check that document for your minimum rates. The Fair Work Commission website has a searchable database of registered agreements.

### Casual loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When calculating annual salary for a casual, use the casual hourly rate in the formula. For example, $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80 per year.

Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to use the timesheet with the casual loading checkbox.

### Superannuation

Superannuation is an additional payment your employer must make into your super fund. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings (from 1 July 2026), up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. So if your annual salary is $52,254.80, your employer contributes an extra $6,270.58 in super, making your total remuneration $58,525.38.

For high earners, super stops once your earnings exceed the maximum contribution base. The Australian Taxation Office sets this limit each year.

### Tax and take-home pay

Your take-home pay depends on your tax bracket and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners).

For the National Minimum Wage annual salary of $52,254.80, the estimated tax is approximately $6,016 (using the 2026–27 scale) plus Medicare of $1,045, leaving a take-home pay of about $45,194 per year, or $869 per week. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

### Fortnightly pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the National Minimum Wage: $1004.90 × 2 = $2009.80 per fortnight. After tax and Medicare, your take-home fortnightly pay would be roughly $1,738.

### Using the timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate. If you are casual, tick the checkbox to add 25% casual loading. The calculator then shows your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax, Medicare, and super. It assumes a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Remember that this is an estimate – actual pay may vary due to unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### Summary

To find your minimum salary in Australia, start with your hourly rate (or the National Minimum Wage of $26.44), multiply by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks. Add casual loading if applicable. Super is paid on top at 12%. Tax and Medicare are deducted from your gross pay. For award-covered employees, check your specific award rate on the [reference tables](/data) page.

Understanding these components helps you compare job offers and budget effectively. Always refer to official sources like the Fair Work Ombudsman, Fair Work Commission, Australian Bureau of Statistics, and Australian Taxation Office for the most current figures.
